reason: E1 shows that O and N interstitials cause phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa RHEA, supporting the first two premises. However, the hypothesis extends this to Ti- and Ni-containing HEAs without evidence that the mechanism applies to Ni-bearing systems or that UHV processing alone ensures a homogeneous single-phase solid solution in the target alloy. The generalization and the efficacy of UHV melting for this specific composition are unsupported.
premises: Oxygen and nitrogen interstitials promote phase segregation during elevated-temperature exposure in refractory HEAs
Interstitial-driven phase segregation depletes the matrix of solute atoms, causing softening
Reducing interstitial impurities prevents segregation and preserves solid-solution strengthening
Ultra-high-vacuum melting effectively minimizes oxygen and nitrogen pickup
The cited TiVNbTa alloy behavior generalizes to Ti- and Ni-containing HEAs
